newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on USDA production estimate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on USDA production estimate.

text.p: A hike by USDA in its outlook for 1996 U.S. corn production pressed CBOT corn futures to a lower close and a new low was set in the September contract, traders said.

"The crop report is bearish, there's no doubt about that and they're looking at the carryout getting even bigger maybe up to 1.2 billion (bushels)," said Paul Haugens, vice president for Chicago-based trade house FIMAT Futures.
USDA Tuesday said the 1996 U.S. corn crop would total 9.265 billion bushels, above an average of analysts' estimates for 9.149 billion.
That tally was well above the government's October outlook for 9.012 billion.
The government also hiked its outlook for 1996-97 U.S. carryout to 1.107 billion bushels from the previous forecast for 903 billion. The marketing year ends on August 30.
Corn was further pressured by an increase in USDA's carryout estimate for other U.S. feedgrains including sorghum, barley and oats.
Corn closed 1/4 to 2-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 1/4 at $2.68. March closed 1-1/4 cents lower at $2.70-1/2.
